subject: Re: POC scope - traffic clarifications & next steps
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@novatek.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-07T14:03:00Z
Subject: Re: POC scope - traffic clarifications & next steps

Hi Laura — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we have alignment before we spin up the pilot pool. I included Ben and Marissa for capacity/ops and trial coordination.

High-level workload profile (what we heard you say):
- Primary API: /v1/complete (instruction-following) + occasional /v1/embed for metadata lookups.
- Steady-state: 8 RPS average across two endpoints (read-heavy), expected 95th around 24 RPS.
- Concurrency expectation: 18 simultaneous open requests during peak business hours.
- Burst pattern: marketing-triggered campaign ~300 RPS spikes for ~90-150s, once every 2-3 days for the first month.
- Tokens: average prompt tokens ~150, expected completion mean ~120 tokens, 95th percentile completion ~850 tokens for long-form generation.

POC success criteria (proposal):
1) Functional: feature parity for responses to a curated eval set (precision QA > 92% on your NLU rubric).
2) Performance: p95 inference latency < 2.5s for standard requests (<= 200 tokens), p95 < 4.5s for long-form (<= 900 tokens) in peak steady-state.
3) Cost: unit cost within target envelope (we'll provide breakouts) and <15% variance vs baseline estimate.
4) Reliability: sustained availability >= 99.5% for the trial window (excluding scheduled maintenance).

Evaluation plan and timeline (draft):
- Week 0 (this week): exchange tokenized sample requests and confirm RPS/concurrency windows (owner: Novatek - Laura).
- Week 1: Redwood will provision a dedicated trial pool (reserved GPUs) and load a mirror of the eval set; run baseline runs. (owner: Ben).
- Week 2: Joint stress tests including the 300 RPS burst scenario; collect latency/cost telemetry. (owners: Ben + Novatek eng).
- Week 3: Quality regression check against your rubric and sign-off meeting. (owner: Marissa + Laura).

Operational notes / assumptions:
- We'll do prefix KV caching for repeated prompts; please mark any requests that must be cold-started.
- For bursts we recommend a temporary autoscale window + fallback model variant to keep latency within SLOs.
- We will need a scoped sample of your heaviest-generation requests (attached sample-tokenized-requests.json).

Immediate asks (can you confirm by EOD Tuesday):
1) Confirm the 300 RPS burst frequency and a realistic maximum duration (you said ~2 minutes on call).
2) Share a small set (50) of representative long-form requests with labels for the 95th token lengths.
3) Point of contact for on-call during stress test (name + cell).

Attachments: novatek-poc-runbook.xlsx (draft runbook), sample-tokenized-requests.json (50 samples), poc-success-matrix.md (scoring matrix draft).

Thanks — I’ll schedule the kickoff once we have those items.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@novatek.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-07T16:21:00Z
Subject: Re: POC scope - traffic clarifications & next steps

Connor — thanks, this is helpful and mirrors our notes. Quick answers inline: 

> Steady-state: 8 RPS average across two endpoints
Yes — that’s accurate for API v1 endpoints. We also have an internal admin endpoint (ad-hoc analytics) that will add ~1.5 RPS sporadically.

> Burst pattern: marketing-triggered campaign ~300 RPS spikes for ~90-150s
Confirmed — marketing typically batches events and we see short, high-volume bursts like this. In the first week we'll likely have two such bursts during business hours.

Tokens:
- Average prompt ~150 tokens; completions vary but the 95th is indeed in the 700-900 token range.

We will: 
- Share 60 long-form samples (with labels) by Tues 09:00 PT. (owner: Laura)
- POC on-call: Miguel Santos (miguel.santos@novatek.com, +1-415-555-0183)

One clarifying question: are you planning to run the 300 RPS bursts against a single model variant or allow fallback to a smaller/quantized variant during burst windows? That will change cost estimates.

-L
Laura Chen
Head of Product Engineering
Novatek Systems
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@novatek.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-08T09:10:00Z
Subject: Re: POC scope - traffic clarifications & next steps

Thanks Laura — good details. A few operational clarifications from the infra side: 

1) Tokenization / tokenizer differences: please confirm whether the token counts were computed with our tokenizer (gpt-ish BPE) or with byte-level counts. We’ll run a cross-check but want to make sure the 95th bucket maps to expected KV cache sizes.

2) Burst handling: we typically recommend a two-tier policy for your use case:
   - Normal: full-precision model (baseline quality) with autoscale target tuned to p95 latency SLOs.
   - Burst fallback: quantized variant (2-3x cheaper) with slightly looser latency but controlled quality checks.

If Novatek wants to force a single-variant policy for fidelity reasons we can size GPUs accordingly but cost will increase ~40% in our estimate.

3) Acceptance thresholds: Connor suggested p95 < 2.5s for <=200 tokens. For the trial we propose a guardrail matrix: p50/p95 <= (0.6s / 2.5s) for short requests; (1.5s / 4.5s) for long-form. If your QA team can accept +/- 10% on those during stress windows, we can mark the test as green.

4) Test harness: I'll provision a reproducible harness (K6 + tokenized samples) and post results to the Drive link. Expect initial baseline runs Wed morning. (owner: Ben).

Next internal step: Connor + I will size the dedicated pool (GPU count, model variants) and share a cost estimate by EOD Wed. Marissa — can you own scheduling the joint stress test (Week 2) and invite Novatek eng?

Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>

Laura / team — great, we're aligned. Final mutual action plan attached and summarized below. I put tentative dates so we can lock calendars.

Mutual Action Plan (draft):
- Tue 2027-06-08 09:00 PT: Novatek delivers 60 long-form samples + tokenization notes (owner: Laura) — received.
- Wed 2027-06-09 08:00 PT: Redwood baseline runs complete; cost and model-variant recommendation sent (owner: Ben) — in progress.
- Mon 2027-06-14: Joint burst stress test (owner: Marissa + Miguel Santos) — calendar invite sent.
- Fri 2027-06-18: Quality sign-off meeting; deliver final success matrix and go/no-go readout (owner: Connor + Laura).

Acceptance and gating:
- Functional pass = >= 92% on Novatek rubric over the eval set.
- Performance pass = within the p95 latency targets above for steady windows; during marketing bursts we accept up to +10% variance if fallback policy engaged.

Attachments enclosed: novatek-poc-runbook.xlsx (updated v1.1), sample-tokenized-requests.json (60 items), poc-success-matrix.md (updated thresholds).

Open question answered: Ben — we will start with a two-variant policy (baseline + quantized fallback). If Novatek later requests single-variant fidelity we will re-evaluate costs.

Next immediate action: Laura — confirm receipt of invite and Miguel's availability for the 6/14 stress test. If we get a thumbs-up today we will lock the cluster provisioning.

Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
